title: Local tensor roof for two augmented resolutions
statement: Let i:Z\to Y be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with additive tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Fix opens V in Z and U in Y, and arbitrary cochain complexes P,K,S on Y [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Write F for termwise open restriction to U, and G for tensor pullback along i followed by restriction to V and its over site W=V intersect i^{-1}(U) [lem-sc-homology-evaluation-formal-complex]. Suppose a:F(P)\to F(S) and b:F(K)\to F(S) are both K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Then there are a complex L on W's over site and quasi-isomorphisms q:L\to G(P), p:L\to G(K) [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. No freeness, zero differential, bound, Koszul sequence, affine chart, or closed immersion hypothesis is assumed. The vertex L may depend on both augmentations.

source.place: Proof of independence of K-flat representatives; Tag 06YI derived pullback and composition with open restriction.

proof.text: The quasi-isomorphisms a and b identify F(P) and F(K) in the standard derived category of U-modules. Factor Q(a) followed by the inverse of Q(b) using Mathlib DerivedCategory.right_fac. Reflect isomorphisms with isIso_Q_map_iff_quasiIso to see that both roof maps s and t are quasi-isomorphisms. Choose a K-flat resolution r:R -> T of the common vertex; r followed by s and r followed by t are quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes.

Put W=V.ι inverse-image of i inverse-image U and g=(V.ι followed by i) restricted over U. Let E be Mathlib Scheme.Modules.overEquiv W and H the termwise functor of tensorPullback g followed by E.inverse. Tensor pullback and open restriction have the same right adjoint, so leftAdjointUniq identifies them for an open immersion. Apply nonempty_tensorPullbackComp, morphismRestrict_ι and overFunctorEquiv W to obtain a natural isomorphism F followed by H -> G. These comparisons are lifted degreewise using NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex. Additivity of tensor pullback follows from its adjunction; E.inverse is additive because it preserves binary biproducts.

Apply tensorPullback_quasiIso_of_isKFlat to r followed by s and r followed by t along g. The inverse equivalence E.inverse is exact, so its functor on complexes preserves both quasi-isomorphisms. Compose these two maps with the P and K components of the natural isomorphism F followed by H -> G. Their common source H(R) and their two quasi-isomorphism properties give the desired witnesses. No nonempty-open assumption is used, and a zero endpoint is allowed precisely when the supplied augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism.

proof_origin.note: Common roof and K-flat vertex replacement are written in Lean. Existing scheme-level tensorPullback_quasiIso_of_isKFlat replaces the lower-level inverse-image/change-of-rings glue. All endpoint comparisons are proved using adjunction uniqueness and the open over-site equivalence; no new holes.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_local_kflat_tensor_roof
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y)
    [(Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).Additive]
    (V : Z.Opens) (U : Y.Opens) (P K S : CochainComplex Y.Modules ℤ) :
    let F := (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let G := (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
      moduleOpenOverComplexFunctor Z V (V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (i ⁻¹ᵁ U))
    ∀ (a : F.obj P ⟶ F.obj S) (b : F.obj K ⟶ F.obj S),
      CochainComplex.IsKFlatResolution (R := U.toScheme.sheaf) a →
      CochainComplex.IsKFlatResolution (R := U.toScheme.sheaf) b →
      ∃ (L : CochainComplex
          (SheafOfModules (V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf.over (V.ι ⁻¹ᵁ (i ⁻¹ᵁ U)))) ℤ)
        (q : L ⟶ G.obj P) (p : L ⟶ G.obj K), QuasiIso q ∧ QuasiIso p
